title: Custom CRM and ERP Development in New York City
metaTitle: Custom CRM and ERP Development in New York City | TDM
metaDescription: Custom CRM and ERP systems for New York City firms: pipelines, inventory, HR, finance, integrations and data migration. Quoted after a free consultation.
lead: TDM (The Digital Marketing Services) builds custom CRM and ERP systems for New York City businesses, working remotely. We design software around the way a company actually sells, stocks, staffs and bills: sales pipelines, inventory and purchasing, HR, finance and operations, connected to the tools already in use. A wholesaler in the Garment District, a property manager in the Bronx and a contractor in Queens each tend to run on their own mix of spreadsheets and group chats, and a system that fits the work removes much of that friction.

sections.heading: Why off-the-shelf software often strains in New York
paragraphs: Many New York companies are small in headcount and complicated in operation. A property management firm does not think in customers and deals. It thinks in buildings, units, tenants, supers, work orders and inspections. Standard CRM products can be bent to fit, but a spreadsheet usually ends up kept on the side.

Then there is cost. Subscription software charges per seat, and that bill grows with every hire, every part-time dispatcher and every field worker who only needs to tick off a job from a phone. For some firms a system they own outright is the cheaper path over several years. We run that comparison with you before any build is proposed, and we say so when buying is the better answer.

sections.heading: What a build covers
paragraphs: Most clients begin with the one or two modules that cause the most trouble and add others later on the same platform. Discovery is done on calls with the people who do the job, so the system reflects real steps.
bullets: CRM: lead capture, pipeline stages, contact histories, task automation and follow-up workflows.
ERP modules for stock and warehouse management, purchasing, payroll and attendance, invoicing and expenses.
Two-way integrations with your website, online store, accounting software, email, payment gateways and logistics providers.
Role-based dashboards showing sales, stock levels, cash position and team workload as they stand today.
Migration from spreadsheets and old software, with records mapped, cleaned, deduplicated and verified against the source.
Granular permissions, audit trails, encryption and backups for sensitive HR and finance data.

sections.heading: Things specific to operating here
paragraphs: Field staff in New York rarely sit at a desk. Technicians, brokers, inspectors and drivers move between boroughs by subway and van, so screens have to work on a phone, with one hand, and cope with a signal that drops underground.

Companies with customers or sites on both sides of the Hudson, or in Westchester and Long Island, deal with different tax rates and rules by location. Firms that hold personal data about New York residents also have state data security obligations, and financial firms regulated by the state have cybersecurity rules of their own. We build access controls, logging and encryption to support the requirements your counsel or compliance officer sets out. We do not give legal advice.

sections.heading: What to ask any developer before signing
paragraphs: Ask who will own the source code and the data. With TDM you own both, and full documentation means another competent team could take the system over. Ask to see a clickable prototype before development begins, since that is the cheapest moment to change anything.

faqs.q: Should my NYC business build a custom CRM or buy one?
faqs.a: Buy when a standard product covers nearly everything you do. Build when your workflows are specific to your trade, or when per-seat fees across a growing team would cost more over a few years than a system you own.

faqs.q: How much does a custom CRM or ERP cost in New York City?
faqs.a: It depends on scope: the number of modules, integrations, users and the state of your existing data. We quote after a free consultation and a discovery stage that defines what will be built.

faqs.q: How do you move our data out of spreadsheets safely?
faqs.a: We export from your current tools, map each field to the new structure, clean and deduplicate the records, and run trial migrations on a staging system that your team checks against the source. The final migration runs only after sign-off.

faqs.q: How long does a CRM or ERP project take?
faqs.a: It depends on your requirements and how many modules are in the first release. Systems are rolled out module by module, and the milestones are agreed in the plan after discovery.
